Intern project kickoff

Build a dental local anaesthesia trainer.

This page explains the exact Phase 1 prototype interns need to build: a desktop training app with case selection, nerve block decision-making, 3D injection site marking, DICOM/CBCT reference support, feedback, and performance tracking.

3Weeks

Project focus

Decision + visual landmark trainer

The app should help a trainee read a clinical case, choose the correct local anaesthesia technique, mark an injection site on a jaw model, and learn from structured feedback.

React UI Three.js viewer FastAPI backend SQLite tracking Doctor-approved JSON MATLAB as support tool

Maverick styling direction

Use a clean healthcare simulation interface inspired by Maverick Simulation Solutions: white and light-blue base, strong blue accents, soft medical grey backgrounds, generous spacing, rounded panels, professional typography, and a calm clinical-product feel. Avoid clutter, dark-heavy dashboards, neon effects, or gaming-style UI.
What interns need to build

Phase 1 prototype scope

  • ✓Case list and patient profile screens
  • ✓Nerve block / technique selection
  • ✓3D jaw model viewer
  • ✓Click-to-coordinate capture
  • ✓CBCT/DICOM reference panel
  • ✓Accuracy feedback screen
  • ✓Performance dashboard

MATLAB recommendation — use it as a support tool

Since both interns are comfortable with MATLAB, they may use it for DICOM/CBCT exploration and image preparation. However, MATLAB should not become the main app stack for the final prototype.

Where MATLAB is useful

  • ✓DICOM / CBCT slice exploration
  • ✓Image preprocessing and contrast adjustment
  • ✓Choosing useful axial / coronal reference slices
  • ✓Exporting PNG reference images for the app
  • ✓Preparing temporary landmark annotations

What remains the final prototype stack

  • 1React for user interface screens
  • 2Three.js for the 3D jaw model viewer
  • 3FastAPI for case logic and validation
  • 4SQLite for storing attempts and scores
  • 5Electron for the desktop wrapper

Important boundary

MATLAB can be used to prepare reference images and explore DICOM data, but the final application should not depend on MATLAB to run. All clinical values, landmarks, injection zones, and feedback text must remain in JSON so the app can run independently.

Recommended MATLAB workflow for interns

Step 1 — Explore

  • Open DICOM / CBCT data in MATLAB.
  • Review axial and coronal slices.
  • Identify useful reference views.

Step 2 — Export

  • Crop and adjust contrast if needed.
  • Export selected slices as PNG files.
  • Place images inside /data/reference_images/.

Step 3 — Use in app

  • React displays the PNG in the DICOM reference panel.
  • FastAPI still handles validation and scoring.
  • JSON remains the source of truth.
MATLAB
  → DICOM / CBCT exploration
  → reference slice selection
  → PNG export
  → React DICOM reference panel

React + Three.js + FastAPI + SQLite + Electron
  → final working desktop prototype

Clinical calibration will be shared after doctor review

The detailed clinical calibration document will be shared with interns after Dr. Tomar / Dr. Mayank fill out the particulars. Until then, interns should build the app using placeholder JSON structures only.

What the final doctor-approved input will provide

  • 1Confirmed nerve blocks to include in v1
  • 2Landmark coordinates on the jaw model
  • 3Injection target centres and tolerance radii
  • 43–5 validated clinical case scenarios
  • 5Clinical feedback language and contraindication rules

Intern instruction

Do not hardcode clinical coordinates, nerve block rules, dosage rules, or feedback messages inside React or Python logic. Keep them in JSON files so they can be replaced once Dr. Tomar / Dr. Mayank approves the final values.

Backend prompt

Create a FastAPI backend for a dental local anaesthesia trainer with health check, case list, case detail, attempt submission, performance summary, and calibration JSON loading.

Frontend prompt

Create a React app for a dental LA training tool with home, case list, patient details, injection trainer, feedback, and performance dashboard pages.

Trainer screen prompt

Create a React trainer screen with a 3D jaw/model viewer area, a DICOM/CBCT reference panel, coordinate display, and submit attempt button.

Validation prompt

Write a Python validation function that reads a calibration JSON, compares clicked coordinates against the expected target centre and tolerance radius, and returns score and feedback.
